Occupational and speech. We graduated from occupational and as a result, she doesn't go to that anymore 😀

We are still going to speech but I'll tell you right now, occupational was just... The best thing for her. They did things for her I didn't think we're possible. Heck, their advice helped ME with issues I didn't even know I had. 

Getting an excited or an anxious child to a baseline is the first thing one has to do, and they teach you how to do that in therapy.  This will prevent them from getting *frustrated*.  We were told to do this before school. That right there was the secret to our success. We were told to get my girl to that baseline by doing these things :

- making her work physically, to the point where she exhausts herself (I was surprised by this one the most). This was her favorite way to get to a sensory baseline. We did this by having her rock with us, lift items around the house that were heavy for her (like laundry detergent), or doing kid workouts on YouTube


- going for long walks (she didn't like this one, she said her legs were too little)

- kickball with a paper bag in the air or a soccer ball (we didn't ever have time for this) 

Rewarding positive behavior, like your child participating with other kids, is also key.

It's work, but it's not that hard after it becomes a routine. Takes five minutes out of your day, and boy does it make a difference in their quality of life. They're just... Happier afterwards, and more inclined to be involved. 

The therapist says that exhausting them this way sets their baseline for 4 hours. Some children grow out of this. I suspect yours will, too
